name: April 15, 2025 Regular Meeting
minutes_text:
MINUTES
  PARKS AND RECREATION COMMISSION
  REGULAR MEETING
  APRIL 15, 2025
  MULTIPURPOSE ROOM
  6:30 P.M.

MEETING CALL TO ORDER

  Chair Skophammer called the meeting t0 order at 6:40 p.m.

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance by the Recording Secretary:

  PRESENT: Chair Dane Skophammer, Vice Chair Alicia Peak, Commissioners Georgia
  Goldfarb, and Judy Villablanca

  ABSENT: Commissioner Jake Lingo

  ALSO PRESENT: Kristin Riesgo, Community Services Director; Chris Orosz, Recreation
  Supervisor; and Brittany Saleaumua, Administrative Assistant

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Chair Skophammer led the Pledge of Allegiance.

APPROVAL OF AGENDA

MOTION  Vice Chair Peak moved, and Commissioner Villablanca seconded a motion to
  approve the agenda. The question was called, and the motion carried 4-0;
  Commissioner Lingo absent.

REPORT ON POSTING OF AGENDA

  Administrative Assistant Saleaumua reported the agenda for the meeting was
  posted on April 10, 2025.

ITEM 1  CEREMONIAL/PRESENTATIONS

  None.

ITEM 2  WRITTEN AND ORAL COMMUNICATIONS FROM THE PUBLIC

  None.

ITEM 3  CONSENT CALENDAR

MOTION  Chair Skophammer moved, and Commissioner Goldfarb seconded a motion to
  approve the agenda. The question was called, and the motion carried 4-0;
  Commissioner Lingo absent.

  The Consent Calendar consisted of the following items:
  A.  Previously Discussed Items
  None.
  B.  New Items
  l.  Approval of Minutes
  Recommended Action: Approve the minutes for the March 18, 2025 Parks
  and Recreation Commission Regular meeting.
  2.  Community Services Department Monthly Report
  Recommended Action: Receive and file a report of activities, events,
  projects, and programs coordinated by the Community Services Department
  in March 2025.

ITEM 4  OLD BUSINESS

  None.

ITEM 5  NEW BUSINESS

  Commission Assignments

  Recommended Action: 1) Review the Parks and Recreation Commission
  assignments for Fiscal Year 2024-25; and 2) Recommend assignments for Fiscal
  Year 2025-26 for City Council consideration.

  Community Services Director Riesgo presented the staff report.

  Chair Skophammer suggested removing assignments that no longer applied or were
  time intensive.

  In response to Chair Skophammer, Community Services Director Riesgo stated the
  Charmlee Park Nature Center was a Capital Improvement Project through Public
  Works and staff would seek feedback from the Commission.

  Vice Chair Peak stated that assignment #8 related to the Charmlee Wilderness Park
  Nature Center should be moved to assignment #13 since it was a lower priority.

  In response to Commissioner Villablanca, Community Services Director Riesgo
  stated that assignment #1 8, exploration of a dog park at Las Flores Creek Park, was
  directed by the Council. She stated Council wanted the Commission to explore the
  dog park option again.

  Page 3 of 6

Commissioner Villablanca stated that the dog park at Las Flores Creek Park was
not feasible due to environmentally sensitive habitat area (ESHA) and the park
layout.

Community Services Director Riesgo stated staff would review options to redesign
areas of the park due to the damage sustained during the Palisades Fire.

Vice Chair Peak stated that the redesign could include a dog park.

Community Services Director Riesgo stated that a consultant would assist with Las
Flores Creek Park redesign.

Vice Chair Peak suggested revising assignment #1 8 to state “Review and provide
feedback regarding the redesign of Las Flores Creek Park.”

In response to Vice Chair Peak, Community Services Director Riesgo stated the
Malibu Bluffs Park Snack Shack design would include meetings with the designer
and youth sports organizations.

In response to Chair Skophammer and Vice Chair Peak, Community Services
Director Riesgo stated the Snack Shack design required community feedback which
was the public process. She stated the Commission should receive the feedback and
narrow the scope of the snack shack design.

Vice Chair Peak suggested planning a Snack Shack community outreach meeting.
She stated the facility benefited the community, and an outreach meeting was
needed.

Chair Skophammer suggested revising assignment #4, related to the
multigenerational recreation center, to match the direction provided by the City
Council at the October 28, 2024 Malibu City Council Regular meeting following
the Community Lands Outreach survey results.

The Commission indicated agreement with Chair Skophammer.

Vice Chair Peak suggested removing assignment three, which related to the
feedback regarding the Malibu Community Lands Outreach survey results, since
that process was completed.

The Commission indicated agreement with Vice Chair Peak.

Vice Chair Peak requested indicating which assignments were ongoing, revised, or
new.
   Parks and Recraation Commission

  Page 4 of 6

  The Commission directed staffto update the year for the Jake Kuredjian Citizenship
  Award assignment, combine assignments #9 and #12 to state “Review the Parks
  Master Plan, make recommendations, and facilitate outreach regarding the priority
  of facilities and amenities at existing and potential future City Parks, and remove
  assignments #16 and #17.

  In response to Vice Chair Peak, Community Services Director Riesgo stated that
  assignment #1 8 would be revised to state “Review and provide feedback regarding
  the redesign of Las Flores Creek Park, including a potential dog park.”

CONSENSUS
  By Consensus, the Commission requested that the proposed assignments including
  1) revising assignment #8 regarding Charmlee Wildemess Park to be assignment
  #13; 2) revise assignment #18 to state “Review and provide feedback on the
  redesign of Las Flores Creek Park, including a potential dog park;” 3) revising
  assignment #4 to state “Provide feedback to staff regarding the development of a
  Request for Proposals (RFP) to create a master plan for a multigenerational sports
  complex to include amenities such as a pool, sports courts, a gymnasium, a senior
  center, and multipurpose spaces for community programs and events with
  preference to placement on the Heathercliff or Ioki parcels;” 4) removing
  assignment #3; 5) revise assignment #11 to state “Nominate and recommend
  recipient(s) for the 2025 Jake Kuredjian Citizenship Award to City Council,” 6)
  combine assignments #9 and #12 to state “Review the Parks Master Plan, make
  recommendations, and facilitate outreach regarding the priority of facilities and
  amenities at existing and potential future City Parks,” 7) remove assignments #16
  and #17; and 8) bring back a final and revised FY 2025-26 assignment item on the
  May 20, 2025 Regular meeting, Consent Calendar for Commission review.

  B.  Earth Friendlv Management Policy

  Recommended Action: 1) Receive and file a report on the Earth Friendly
  Management Policy activities from July 2024 through March 2025; and 2) Review
  and approve the use of Pyrethrum Concentrate, which will be applied at City Hall
  and the Michael Landon Center.

  Recreation Supervisor Orosz presented the staff report.

  Vice Chair Peak suggested installing pollinator garden signs at City parks to help
  raise awareness for park visitors.

  In response to Commissioner Goldfarb, Recreation Supervisor Orosz stated that the
  Pyrethrum Concentrate solution would only be applied to the interior of the
  building since an exterior application would be toxic to over 100 insects.
   Parks and Recreation Commission

  In response to Commissioner Goldfarb, Recreation Supervisor Orosz stated that the
  Terro Ant Bait Solution was not OMRI-approved.

  In response to Chair Skophammer, Recreation Supervisor Orosz stated that
  multiple applications of the Pyrethrum Concentrate would be necessary throughout
  the summer due to increased ant activity and would then be applied annually during
  the Spring and Summer seasons as needed.

MOTION  Vice Chair Peak moved, and Chair Skophammer seconded a motion to approve the
  application of the Pyrethrum Concentrate at Malibu City Hall and the Michael
  Landon Center. The question was called, and the motion carried 4—0; Commissioner
  Lingo absent.

  Commissioner Goldfarb recommended reviewing other options that could reduce
  the ant infestation at City facilities.

ITEM 6  STAFF UPDATES

  Recreation Supervisor Orosz provided an update on Charmlee Wilderness Park and
  trail maintenance.

  Community Services Director Riesgo provided an update on Aquatics programs,
  Senior Center programs, Day Camps, Afterschool programs, Workshops,
  Permanent Skate Park, Community Lands, and Department recruitments.

  In response to. Vice Chair Peak, Chair Skophammer stated keeping the Temporary
  Skate Park open would delay the construction of the Permanent Skate Park.

  In response to Commissioner Goldfarb, Community Services Director Riesgo
  stated that the Temporary Skate Park would be inspected. She stated that if it were
  in good condition, the equipment would be publicly sold.

ITEM 7  COMMISSIONER REPORTS, COMMENTS AND INQUIRIES

  Commissioner Villablanca stated that the Permanent Skate Park groundbreaking
  event was well done.

  Commissioner Goldfarb stated that the Malibu Monarch Proj ect printed posters and
  trading cards related to Malibu’s native habitats, flora, and fauna. She stated Sandy
  Glover was the artist and the organization planned to distribute the items to the
  community.
